notes:
Top-line: Opaline Rail Systems (mid-to-large global rail operator) evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for operations chat + maintenance workflows. Primary driver: keep PII/telemetry inside their VPC and meet EU/UK data residency for certain telemetry and maintenance logs.

Summary of needs:
- Must deploy in customer-managed VPC with private endpoints; no public internet ingress to model endpoints.
- KMS integration required: customer-managed keys (OK with AWS KMS CMK). Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) required for prod.
- Audit logging & retention: 7 years for certain incident logs; want near-real-time log export to their SIEM (Splunk).
- SSO: SAML2.0 integration for console access + RBAC.
- Network topology: prefer Transit Gateway hub-and-spoke; VPN and DirectConnect options for on-prem datacenters. Expected to use peering for EU region.
- Inbound/outbound constraints: only outbound to Redwood control plane on predefined egress IPs/ports (need list). No inbound open ports.
- Regions: primary NA region (us-west-2), EU fallback (eu-west-1) for residency; question about latency for on-boarded models and GPU colocated options.
- Runtime requirements: preference for pinned model versions, support for quantized variants for cost; batch window for low-latency routing on dispatch.

- Audit logging: must support streaming of request/response metadata (not full PII) to Splunk; retention and redaction rules discussed.
- VPC topology: propose hub Transit Gateway in each region, VPC peering for on-prem, PrivateLink for control-plane calls, NATs for egress to Redwood update endpoints. Customer may prefer no NAT and only allow egress through managed proxy — will need to validate.
- Fallbacks: customer wants policy to failover to EU-region model only when data flagged for EU residency; careful about routing to lower-cost variants in other regions.
- Performance: latency SLO for chat is 150-250ms P95 for short prompts; discussing dedicated GPU pool for critical routes.
